감기에 걸리다.example: 감기에 걸려서 오늘 수업에 못 갔어요.
감기에 걸리다.exampleEn: I caught a cold, so I could not go to class today.
감기에 걸리다.originNote: 한자어 기반 표현. 감기 is written with Hanja 感氣, while modern Mandarin normally uses 感冒.

아프다.exampleEn: My head hurts / I have a headache.

몸조리.exampleEn: If you caught a cold, take good care of yourself.
몸조리.originNote: 혼종어: 몸 is native Korean; 조리 comes from 調理.

열이 나다.exampleEn: I have a fever, so I am resting at home.

배가 고프다.exampleEn: I was hungry, so I ate gimbap.

시끄럽다.exampleEn: The dorm is too noisy at night.

빨래하다.exampleEn: I have to do laundry on the weekend.

바꾸다.exampleEn: May I speak to Minsu? / Please put Minsu on the phone.

빌리다.exampleEn: I borrowed a book from the library.

빌려주다.exampleEn: I will lend you an umbrella.

부치다.exampleEn: I mailed a letter at the post office.

끊다.exampleEn: Then I will hang up first.

전화번호.exampleEn: Please tell me your phone number.
전화번호.originNote: 한자어. 전화 = 電話, 번호 = 番號. Modern Mandarin normally says 电话号码.

메시지.exampleEn: The call did not go through, so I left a message.

통화중이다.example: 지금 통화중이에요. 조금 후에 다시 전화해 주세요.
통화중이다.exampleEn: The line is busy now. Please call again a little later.
통화중이다.originNote: 통화 = 通話, 중 = 中. A compact Sino-Korean expression meaning ‘in the middle of a call.’

이따가.exampleEn: Let’s meet at the library a little later.

다시.exampleEn: Sorry, but please say it again.

눈.example: 눈이 아파서 컴퓨터를 오래 못 봐요.
눈.exampleEn: My eyes hurt, so I cannot look at the computer for long.

코.exampleEn: I caught a cold, so my nose is stuffy.

이.exampleEn: My tooth hurts, so I have to go to the dentist.

목.example: 목이 아파서 말을 많이 못 해요.
목.exampleEn: My throat hurts, so I cannot talk much.

어깨.exampleEn: My shoulder hurts, so I want to rest.

허리.exampleEn: My lower back hurts because I sat for a long time.

다리.exampleEn: My legs hurt because I walked a lot.

발.exampleEn: My feet hurt because of small shoes.

도시.originNote: 한자어. The same characters 都市 are also used in Chinese, though 城市 is more common in everyday Mandarin.

반.originNote: 한자어. 半 means ‘half’ in both Korean Hanja vocabulary and Chinese.

뉴스.exampleEn: I watched the news in the morning.

감기.exampleEn: I could not go to school because of a cold.
감기.originNote: 한자어. The Hanja is 感氣; modern Mandarin uses 感冒 for ‘a cold.’

물가.exampleEn: Prices have gone up a lot these days.
물가.originNote: 한자어. 物價 corresponds closely to modern Chinese 物价.

전화.originNote: 한자어. 電話 corresponds directly to simplified Chinese 电话.
